methods.name: Layer attention rollout
methods.summary: Combine compatible attention matrices across layers into an approximate connectivity view, using explicit head reduction and residual treatment.
methods.question: What connectivity does this compatible layer-chain approximation imply?
methods.definition: Compose compatible head-mean square matrices with declared residual identity coefficient and row normalization: Â_l = r·I + (1−r)·mean_h A_l, rows renormalized over the valid key domain; rollout through layer L is Â_L·…·Â_0, read at the selected source row.

literature_relation.note: Abnar & Zuidema (2020) rollout. Matches at residual coefficient 0.5, with every head averaged over complete aligned matrices; other residual coefficients are extensions.

parameters_schema.description: `layer` is the last layer composed; rollout always starts at layer 0 and averages every query head.
parameters_schema.title: RolloutParameters

output.support: aligned layer position domain
output.normalization: declared row normalization after residual addition

comparison_constraints: Same topology, head reduction, residual rule and layer interval.
limitations: Selected rows/rectangular cross-attention are incompatible; not complete information flow.
All query heads are averaged with equal weight; value vectors, MLPs and layer norms are ignored, so rollout is a routing proxy, not attribution or causation.
Retriever encodings cover the language transformer only; vision-tower attention is not part of the chain.

methods.name: Integrated gradients attribution
methods.summary: Attribute a specified model output to differentiable inputs relative to a declared baseline and integration path. This is output attribution, not attention.
methods.question: What attribution is assigned along a declared input-baseline path for this target?
methods.definition: Path-integrated input gradients times input-minus-baseline, with explicit target and numerical approximation, computed in float32: (x − x′)·(1/m)·Σ_k ∂F(x′ + α_k(x − x′))/∂x with α_k = (k + ½)/m. F is the log-probability of a saved capture's predicted token at one step under teacher forcing; x are the consumed visual-token embeddings entering the language model and x′ the vision encoder's output for a constant black or white image of the consumed size; per-token values sum the embedding dimensions.

step.description: Captured prediction step whose token log-probability is attributed.
step.title: Step

steps.description: Midpoint Riemann steps along the straight input-baseline path.
steps.title: Riemann steps

baseline.description: Constant RGB image of the consumed size; its vision-encoder output is the baseline embedding.
baseline.title: Baseline image

output.support: declared differentiable input axes
output.normalization: baseline/path-dependent

comparison_constraints: Same output target, baseline, path and approximation.
limitations: Not universal model support; token IDs are not differentiable inputs.
Output attribution for the declared target and baseline, not attention; a different baseline or target gives a different attribution.

Forward and backward passes run in float32 on the checkpoint weights upcast exactly from BF16; BF16 arithmetic cannot resolve the path integral. Logits can differ slightly from the BF16 capture; the target is re-checked as the float32 greedy token.
The path integrand can oscillate strongly for vision-language models; completeness and the interleaved half-rule disagreement are reported with every result.
Requires free GPU memory for float32 weights (about 4 bytes per parameter plus activations); larger generators are refused.

Pinned built-in Qwen2-VL and Qwen2.5-VL generators with image inputs only; text and earlier output tokens are held fixed. DeepStack generators (Qwen3-VL) are refused because their visual features also enter later decoder layers.
The vision encoder is outside the integral: attribution is to the visual-token embeddings it produced, not to pixels. The pixel path did not converge on a tested capture by 512 steps.
validation_evidence: library/tests/methods/test_planned_methods.py: midpoint rule exactness on quadratic and completeness on non-separable fixtures; aggregation and experiment-lineage checks. Real-capture completeness is reported per result.

scripts/completed_methods_check.py on saved single-page captures (RTX 4090, 128 steps, black baseline): Qwen2.5-VL-3B step 0 relative completeness gap 0.36% with half rules 1.932/1.925 nats and the embedding forward equal to the native pixel forward; Qwen2-VL-2B step 0 gap 0.0013%; Qwen2.5-VL-3B teacher-forced step 1 gap 1.3% with a 5.6% half-rule disagreement, which the result flags. Qwen3-VL is refused.

methods.name: Element attention profile
methods.summary: Every captured layer and query head's attention from the shown source to each mapped element, as mass, within-image share and area-adjusted enrichment. Opened from Details › Element for the selected element.
methods.question: Which captured layers and query heads allocate the most attention from the selected source to a document element?
methods.definition: M(l,h,e) = sum_j A(s,l,h,j) w(e,j) for every captured layer l and query head h of one source row s; within-image share M/I(l,h); area-relative ratio (M/I)/area share(e).
